title: Present-tense changes
subtitle: Choose a form that fits the person
objectives: Use frequent stem-changing verbs in a routine.
Distinguish yo-only irregularity from a stem change.
Ask a follow-up about a person’s schedule.
warmup: Retrieve two sentences and one repair strategy from c1-u12. Change the subject or situation in each sentence and explain what changed. Then read today’s objectives and predict where your existing language may be insufficient.

lectures.title: Patterns with limits
lectures.body: Present-tense stem changes normally affect stressed stems, excluding nosotros and vosotros: pienso, piensas, piensa, pensamos, pensáis, piensan. With volver, o changes to ue: vuelvo but volvemos. With pedir, e changes to i: pido but pedimos. Not every e or o changes; learn a verb’s pattern with its infinitive. Yo-only changes include hago, pongo, salgo, conozco and sé. Some verbs combine irregularities: tengo but tienes; digo but dices. Do not infer nosotros vuelvemos from vuelvo. Build a short subject-and-action phrase before adding details. You can recognize vosotros even when your normal plural address is ustedes.

lectures.title: Two kinds of knowing
lectures.body: Saber commonly expresses facts or knowing how: Sé la respuesta; sé nadar. Conocer commonly expresses acquaintance with people or places: Conozco a Elena; conozco Quito. The personal a usually marks a specific human direct object: Visito a mi hermana, but visito el museo. It does not turn that person into an indirect object. Ask ¿Sabes dónde está? for information, and ¿Conoces a la profesora? for acquaintance. A useful conversation follows the answer with a relevant detail: ¿A qué hora vuelves? Avoid reciting a paradigm when your partner needs a time or a reason.

lectures.title: Use a paradigm to solve a conversation problem
lectures.body:
Imagine that a colleague asks, **¿A qué hora vuelven ustedes?** You plan to return at six. Begin with **Volvemos a las seis**, because your answer changes the perspective from “you all” to “we.” The stem therefore returns to **volv-**. Copying *vuelven* from the question would keep the wrong subject. If you answer only for yourself, choose **Vuelvo a las seis** instead. The time stays the same; the speaker group changes.

Compare three small families aloud: **pienso → pensamos**, **vuelvo → volvemos**, **pido → pedimos**. Now add a negative, a time and a follow-up: **No volvemos hoy. Volvemos mañana. ¿A qué hora sales tú?** A useful paradigm is a tool for changing a message, not an isolated list. When you encounter a new verb, record its infinitive, yo form and nosotros form. Those three forms often expose both the change and its limit.

Regional recognition has the same purpose. A speaker might ask **¿A qué hora volvés?** with voseo. Understand the question without “correcting” the speaker into tú. Use your practiced variety consistently and notice your interlocutor’s forms.

reading: Lucía trabaja en una librería. Abre a las nueve, pero ella llega antes porque quiere preparar los pedidos. Los lunes vuelve a casa a las seis. Su colega Andrés pide ayuda con un cliente: «No conozco esta novela. ¿Sabes quién la escribió?». Lucía responde: «Sé el nombre de la autora, pero no conozco su obra completa». Después hablan del horario. «¿Podemos salir temprano el viernes?», pregunta Andrés. Lucía piensa un momento: «Podemos, si terminamos los pedidos». Identifica una forma con cambio de raíz, una forma irregular solo en yo y una distinción entre saber y conocer.

worked.reason: Nosotros retains the unstressed o; vuelvemos incorrectly extends the stem change.
The yo form sé is irregular and keeps its accent; conozco would suggest acquaintance.
Pedir changes e to i in this stressed singular stem.
Conocer uses conozco for yo; personal a introduces the known person.
The stressed stem changes e to ie; the second verb stays infinitive.
A specific person as direct object normally takes personal a.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: I think about the schedule.
quiz.explanation: “Pienso en el horario” expresses “I think about the schedule”. “Hago los pedidos” instead means “I prepare the orders”. “¿A qué hora vuelves?” instead means “What time do you return?”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: We return at six.
quiz.explanation: “Volvemos a las seis” expresses “We return at six”. “Visito a mi hermana” instead means “I visit my sister”. “Pongo los libros aquí” instead means “I put the books here”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: I ask for help.
quiz.explanation: “Pido ayuda” expresses “I ask for help”. “Salgo temprano” instead means “I leave early”. “Conocemos el barrio” instead means “We know the neighborhood”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: I know how to swim.
quiz.explanation: “Sé nadar” expresses “I know how to swim”. “Digo la verdad” instead means “I tell the truth”. “Pienso en el horario” instead means “I think about the schedule”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: I know Elena.
quiz.explanation: “Conozco a Elena” expresses “I know Elena”. “Volvemos a las seis” instead means “We return at six”. “¿A qué hora vuelves?” instead means “What time do you return?”.

quiz.prompt: Match each English meaning to its Spanish expression. Use each expression once.
quiz.explanation: “Conozco a Elena” means “I know Elena”. “Podemos salir” means “We can leave”. “Hago los pedidos” means “I prepare the orders”. Each alternative belongs to a different meaning; check the whole phrase, including its grammatical person and register.

homework.prompt: Read the original text for this unit. Identify its situation, central message, and three supporting details. Then write a new version of 100–140 words for a different person or audience. Use the target patterns, change at least three facts, and explain two revisions.
homework.model:
Lucía trabaja en una librería. Abre a las nueve, pero ella llega antes porque quiere preparar los pedidos. Los lunes vuelve a casa a las seis. Su colega Andrés pide ayuda con un cliente: «No conozco esta novela. ¿Sabes quién la escribió?». Lucía responde: «Sé el nombre de la autora, pero no conozco su obra completa». Después hablan del horario. «¿Podemos salir temprano el viernes?», pregunta Andrés. Lucía piensa un momento: «Podemos, si terminamos los pedidos». Identifica una forma con cambio de raíz, una forma irregular solo en yo y una distinción entre saber y conocer.

This is the source model, not a text to submit unchanged. A successful adaptation retains the communicative purpose while changing relevant forms and facts. Compare with the worked examples for the reasons behind form choices.
homework.rubric: 0–3 each: fulfills the specified purpose; organized and comprehensible; target forms support meaning; revisions are explained with examples. 0 = no evidence, 1 = substantial help needed, 2 = effective with some support, 3 = independently effective for this task. Record who evaluated the work.

homework.prompt: Complete the resource assignment, or ask a willing reader to read the original text without showing it to you. First listen for the situation and purpose; listen again for three details and one contrast. Write a 60–100-word listening log naming the source, words actually heard, one uncertainty, and how you checked it. If using local synthesized speech, label it synthetic. Text-only preparation is not completed listening.
homework.model: A useful log separates the speaker’s message from your interpretation: “I heard [specific phrase]; I understood [claim]; I was uncertain about [word/relationship]; checking [text or partner] changed my interpretation to [correction].” Use the unit reading as an answer reference for a read-aloud version, never as evidence of an external speaker’s words.
homework.rubric: 0–2 each: identifies source and listening conditions; retrieves central meaning; supports three details; checks a specific uncertainty. Do not count a copied transcript as independent comprehension.

homework.prompt: Compare two work or study schedules. Ask three genuine follow-ups and agree when you can meet. Include one fact you know and one person or place you know.
homework.model: Use the original reading/dialogue and the sentence-pattern cards as preparation. Make a brief outline, then put it away. Your partner should introduce a detail you did not prepare. Respond, request clarification if needed, and summarize what you agreed or still disagree about. Solo fallback: record two possible viewpoints and improvise a response after a pause; label it rehearsal.
homework.rubric: 0–3 each: task fulfillment, comprehensibility, control of target language, responsiveness to another speaker. A partner or instructor should cite one example per score. Solo rehearsal provides no evidence for live responsiveness; mark that dimension not observed.

homework.prompt: On a later day, retrieve six cards without looking. Use three in a fresh response to the practical task. Identify one recurring form error and one communication difficulty. Produce a corrected example, explain the reason, and schedule a specific follow-up exchange or listening session.
homework.model: Compare your response with these two models: Pienso en el horario / Volvemos a las seis. A useful reflection explains the function, not just the spelling. Revisit the first worked item and create a different example of its principle.
homework.rubric: Report recall count separately from performance. Reflection is complete when it contains an observed difficulty, an explained correction, a fresh example, and an actionable next session.

task: Compare two work or study schedules. Ask three genuine follow-ups and agree when you can meet. Include one fact you know and one person or place you know.
culture: Voseo patterns differ by region: forms such as pensás and volvés are ordinary local usage. Do not assume the stressed tú diphthong appears in a voseo form. Follow the community’s paradigm consistently.
selfAssessment: I can use frequent stem-changing verbs in a routine.
I can distinguish yo-only irregularity from a stem change.
I can ask a follow-up about a person’s schedule.
remediation: Sort mistakes by form, meaning, and interaction. For form errors, explain a worked example and create a contrasting pair. For comprehension errors, replay a short segment or use a willing reader and verify your interpretation. For interaction difficulties, repeat the practical task with one new constraint. Compare evidence across days; repeated selection of a known answer alone is not mastery.
